Port a discharge analysis to easyNIS

Source: vignettes/porting.Rmd
porting.Rmd
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

The examples use invented data.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  select(nis_vars_design(), nis_vars_dx(), AGE, LOS, DIED)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

design <- nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I509") |>
  nis_design(cohort = AGE >= 18 & heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, LOS, DIED))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.

summarise(design, discharges = survey_total(), mean_los = survey_mean(LOS))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1       26.5          5.47     4.92       0.562

Use the full annual input when building the design. Move eligibility conditions from your row filter to cohort. Retain YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT with the analysis columns.

Match within diagnosis slots 

discharges <- nis |>
  select(I10_DX1, I10_DX2) |>
  head(3) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(I10_DX1 = c("I50", "I509", "E119"),
         I10_DX2 = c("9", "E119", "I5022"))

discharges |>
  mutate(legacy = grepl("I509", paste0(I10_DX1, I10_DX2), fixed = TRUE)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(exact = list(regex = "I509"),
              substring = list(regex = ".*50.*"))

#> 3 E119    I5022   FALSE  FALSE TRUE

I509 appears on the first row only after the two slots are pasted together. An exact code pattern checks each slot separately. A substring pattern needs .* on either side of the text you want to match. Compare counts before adopting the new definition. If several legacy category rules match one discharge, keep their original precedence when you recode.

Switch systems when both layouts are present 

transition <- nis_open(nis_example(2015)) |>
  mutate(DX1 = if_else(DQTR < 4 & HOSP_NIS %% 2L == 0L, "4280", DX1),
         I10_DX1 = if_else(DQTR == 4 & HOSP_NIS %% 2L == 0L, "I509", I10_DX1))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Experimental: years before 2016 store ICD-9-CM codes in DX1, PR1, ... slots.
#> ℹ Flag them with `system = "icd9"`; 2015 mixes ICD-9 (Q1-Q3) and ICD-10 (Q4)
#>   slots.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
slots <- colnames(transition)
c(icd9 = "DX1" %in% slots, icd10 = "I10_DX1" %in% slots)
#>  icd9 icd10 
#>  TRUE  TRUE

transition |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf = list(icd9 = "4280", icd10 = "I509"), system = "both") |>
  count(DQTR, hf) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>    DQTR hf        n
#>   <int> <lgl> <dbl>
#> 1     2 FALSE    12
#> 2     3 TRUE     12
#> 3     1 FALSE    12
#> 4     4 TRUE     12
#> 5     3 FALSE    12
#> 6     2 TRUE     12
#> 7     4 FALSE    12
#> 8     1 TRUE     12

q4 <- transition |> filter(DQTR == 4) |> select(-matches("^DX[0-9]+$"))
q4 |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf = "I509", system = "icd10") |>
  count(hf) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   hf        n
#>   <lgl> <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE    12
#> 2 TRUE     12

Use system = "both" when the query contains separate ICD-9 and ICD-10 slots. Use system = "icd10" for an extract with only ICD-10 slots. Years and coding eras

Recode on the appropriate side of the survey design 

source <- nis_open(nis_example(2019)) |>
  mutate(payer_code = PAY1)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpeCp0F5/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

recoded <- nis_design(source, AGE >= 18, keep = c(PAY1, payer_code)) |>
  mutate(payer_group = case_when(
    PAY1 %in% c("Medicare", "Medicaid") ~ "Public",
    !is.na(PAY1) ~ "Other known payer",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
recoded$variables |> select(payer_code, PAY1, payer_group) |> head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   payer_code PAY1                  payer_group      
#>        <int> <fct>                 <chr>            
#> 1          3 Private including HMO Other known payer
#> 2          4 Self-pay              Other known payer
#> 3          5 No charge             Other known payer
#> 4          6 Other                 Other known payer
#> 5          1 Medicare              Public           
#> 6          2 Medicaid              Public

Copy a raw field to a new name while the query is still in DuckDB. nis_design() labels the recognized PAY1 field. Use those labels in the study recode after the design is in R. Keep the raw code when reconciling results against the original extract.

Match the original definition before comparing estimates

In the original analysis In easyNIS
Principal diagnosis only nis_flag_dx(position = "principal")
Exact code I509 list(regex = "^I509$")
ICD-9-CM 4280 and ICD-10-CM I509 Separate code sets with system = "both"
Weighted count survey_total()
Sampled count unweighted(n())

Compare eligibility counts, the original and revised weights, and the standard errors. A matching weighted total can hide a difference in how the design handles hospitals with no cases. How the NIS survey design works

Compare the billed amount, adjusted charge, and estimated cost separately when porting a cost outcome. Record the source charge field, cost-to-charge ratio, CPI series, and reference dollar year before comparing the two analyses. Derive outcomes, comorbidities, and costs
